findings.summary: A completed email change kept every other session alive. Revocation ran after commit as a best-effort call whose failure was only logged, so a failure left old sessions usable for the new address.
findings.remediation: Revocation and replacement session are part of the change transaction (email-change-requests.ts verify). email-change-requests.integration.test.ts asserts rollback on failure and full revocation on success; email-otp.integration.test.ts asserts the old cookie, the other device and the replacement.

files.observations: Read in full (290 lines). Owner decision implemented: on completion, every session of the account is revoked in the same transaction as the address change, and the replacement session is created by the caller through onCompleted, inside that transaction. A failure in the replacement rolls back the change, so the account never holds a new address without a session for it. Single-use codes and replay refusal were already in place. Concurrent completion is serialised by the user row lock taken at the start of verify. Finding S1-F012: completion left the other sessions alive (previously a best-effort call after commit that could fail silently).

Read in full. RFC 4226 HOTP and RFC 6238 step matching use constant-time comparison per candidate and a ±1 drift window. Base32 encode and decode are bounded for the 20-byte secret. Decryption throws on tag mismatch, which is the intended failure. No finding.
